Label: Molded part
Tip: The part to mold (SLDPRT, STEP, IGES, Parasolid). Leave empty if the part is already in this file, or if you only have its drawing (the agent then models the part from the drawing first). It is inserted as a linked Insert Part, so a revised part can be swapped later with Smart Rebuild. STL can't be used.

Label: Engineering drawing
Tip: PDF, image or SolidWorks drawing of the part: tolerances, critical or cosmetic surfaces, flash class, finish. Keep PDFs under 20 MB. DXF/DWG: export a PDF instead.

Label: Critical faces (no parting line)
Tip: If the part is already in this file: faces no parting line, flash, vent or sprue may touch. Otherwise the agent asks you to pick them after it inserts the part.

Label: Mold material
Tip: Aluminium plates with steel inserts for fragile or wearing features, or tool steel throughout. Above about 150 degC (300 degF) aluminium loses strength over time; the agent will recommend steel.

Label: Plate grade
Tip: Grade of the machined plates. Strength is derated for long service (10,000 h) at the press temperature.

Label: Insert grade
Tip: Steel for inserts at fragile, thin or wearing features and for stop pads in an aluminium mold.

Text: {mold_grade.name}: full strength to {mold_grade.max_service_C.full_strength|temperature}, derated to {mold_grade.max_service_C.derated|temperature}, never above {mold_grade.max_service_C.never_above|temperature}

Label: Part material
Tip: Material family of the molded part. Picking a grade loads typical process data into the Process data fields; replace them with your datasheet values. v1 builds molds for liquid pour (PU, epoxy, polyester) and rubber / compound compression; thermoplastic and sinter families get an advisory plan only.

Label: Grade
Tip: Grade or hardness within the family. Its typical values fill the Process data fields below.

Text: Shrink {shrink_pct|percent}, SG {sg}, cure {cure_min|time}, mold {press_temp|temperature} - edit under Process data

Label: Shrinkage
Tip: Linear mold shrinkage. Say below what it was measured on; the agent applies the matching formula and the mold-metal correction.

Label: Shrinkage measured as
Tip: Filled from the grade. Supplier datasheet: cold part vs a cold steel mold (the agent corrects for aluminium and temperature). Measured in my molds: your own value at this temperature (no metal correction). Hot cavity to cold part: contraction from the hot mold. v1 style: cavity = part x (1 + S), only to match molds built with the old tool.
Choices: Measured in my molds at this temperature

Label: Specific gravity
Tip: Density relative to water (molded density for foams). Sets the charge weight.

Label: Mixed viscosity
Tip: Initial mixed viscosity at the processing temperature. Sets the flash-gap class, land and vent depth.

Label: Mooney viscosity
Tip: ML(1+4) at 100 degC, for rubber compounds.

Label: Pot life
Tip: Working time after mixing (days for one-part systems such as LSR or plastisol). All cavities must be poured within half of it.

Label: Cure / demold time
Tip: Demold time at the material's typical mold temperature (datasheet).

Label: Minimum draft
Tip: Smallest draft the part may have on cavity walls.

Label: Molding pressure on the part
Tip: Pressure the material needs on its projected area (datasheet). Sets the press force for compression materials and the design pressure for pours.

Label: Charge excess
Tip: Material added above the part weight so the cavity fills; it leaves as flash. Sets the charge and the overflow volume.

Label: What you set on the press
Tip: Gauge reading: the hydraulic gauge on the press (most common). On the part: pressure on the part's projected area, as material sheets quote it. Force reading: a gauge scale in tons. Not sure: the agent asks.

Label: Gauge pressure
Tip: The number you set or read on the hydraulic gauge.

Label: Pressure on the part
Tip: Pressure on the part's projected area (cavities + land).

Label: Force reading
Tip: The press force you set, read on a tonnage scale.

Label: Press rated force
Tip: Nameplate tonnage. With the gauge reading at that tonnage it gives the ram area, the press-too-small check and the gauge setting for the operator.

Label: Gauge at rated force
Tip: Gauge reading when the press makes its rated force (nameplate or manual). With a gauge that reads force, leave the default: the setup sheet then gives forces.

Label: Press temperature
Tip: Platen set point. Filled from the material; edit it to your process.

Label: Heated platen size
Tip: Usable heated area of the platen (length x width). Unchecked: the footprint check is skipped.

Label: Daylight
Tip: Largest opening between the platens. Unchecked: the stack-height check is skipped.

Label: Stroke
Tip: Ram travel. A mold thinner than daylight minus stroke can't be clamped and needs a riser plate. Unchecked: not checked.

Label: Between cycles the mold
Tip: Slide in and out: the lid comes off on a table each cycle, so lid and base run at different temperatures (sets the dowel scheme and the lifting limit).
Choices: Slides in and out each cycle
Default: Slides in and out each cycle

Label: The mold sits
Tip: Flat on the platen: plates are backed by the platens and don't bend. On a carrier or rails: spans are checked for bending.

Label: Cycle life (parts per cavity)
Tip: Shots the mold must survive. Sets fatigue design, wear parts and thread inserts.

Label: Max weight per machined plate
Tip: Default 23 kg (51 lb): the NIOSH load constant, for plates lifted now and then. Heavier pieces are split or get hoist holes.

Label: Max size per plate
Tip: Largest blank your machine and fixturing take. Compared sorted, so the plate may be turned; blank allowance is added.

Label: Max total base weight
Tip: Total of all base pieces (slid in and out together). Unchecked: not checked.

Label: Max lid weight (your own limit)
Tip: The lid is lifted every cycle, hot. Unchecked: the limit comes from the NIOSH lifting equation and the three answers below (11 kg / 25 lb when the place is not known). Checked: your own limit.

Label: Lid is lifted
Tip: Where the operator lifts the lid off every cycle. Inside the press means a longer reach (at least 55 cm counts) and gloves, so a lower limit. Not sure: 11 kg (25 lb).

Label: Reach to the lid
Tip: Horizontal distance from the operator's ankles to the hands on the lid handles at the start of the lift. Inside the press the agent uses at least 550 mm (22 in).

Label: Lid lifts per hour
Tip: Roughly how many times an hour the lid is lifted (one per cycle, plus any extra handling).

Label: Big decisions
Tip: Ask on big ones: decides routine calls, asks before anything that changes function, cost, the operator's work or the part. Ask about all: asks before every judgement call. Decide everything: makes the calls itself and reports each one.

Label: Notes
Tip: Anything the agent should know: customer requirements, press quirks, how you demold, how your dowels are fitted.
